keyFindings.description: The warn gate lets a disagreement spend the one merge-waiting notice, and the notice then says the opposite of what the daemon is about to do. A ghautomerge.Lagging - GitHub showing the pull request closed, or at another head than the record awaits - is a wait (ghautomerge.go:271), and permanentRefusal answers false for it until it is Stalled (outbox.go:420, Lagging.Stalled at ghautomerge.go:276 bounds that at LagBound). So a row past mergeWaitWarn that meets a fresh disagreement satisfies every term of the gate and emits merge-waiting, whose reason renders that cause as 'GitHub last answered' under the sentence 'The merge has not been withdrawn, the issue stays in awaiting_merge and the daemon goes on submitting it'. Two things are then wrong at once: the notice tells the architect the merge stands while quoting GitHub saying its pull request is closed, and within LagBound the same row ends and sends merge-stalled saying the daemon stopped submitting - two tellings about one row, the second contradicting the first, on an issue whose subject is a record that says what is not so. The doc comment anticipates only the stalled half. One clause closes it: exclude a Lagging cause from warn as well, so a disagreement never spends the notice.

keyFindings.description: It states the head's CI as a present fact and the body contradicts it. 'No CI verdict exists for this head yet, and its absence is not a pass' and 'The last head whose base-required set was read complete and green is the code head b2350b438c51' were both true when written at 2adb7d20 and are false now: I read 2adb7d20's own check runs this round and every required name's newest run is complete and successful there, and the tester's own block in the same body records the same thing. So the ledger the architect reads at acceptance and the merger quotes disagrees with itself, which is the shape round nine found in Proven by. The same paragraph also carries 'cited by run id and never by head' as a rule - the instruction the architect withdrew at 16:33Z after checking it from a pod, on the ground that a run id naming the head's present condition is the record this issue deletes. Scope the first clause to the completion that wrote it, re-derive or drop the superlative, and take the withdrawn rule out.

settledNotReopened: The code-quality half proposed again that the CI-line guard drop its verb grammar for a bare mention pin, on the ground that the bare form matches nothing in the tree today and closes three of the four holes the comment names. I am not carrying it as a finding. The architect ruled in round four that the guard may fire on the instruction and not on any mention, and in round five the implementer gave the reason I accepted on the record: zero hits today is the state of the tree, not a property of the rule, and a skill that must one day say the line is gone would be refused by a ban that cannot tell the two apart. The pair's re-proposal rests on the same measurement that reason already answered. Its live half - that the negation lookbehind does not compose with the re- prefix, so 'never re-writes the CI line' matches - is real, fails closed as a red lane rather than a silent pass, and is disclosed on the body's risk list and the fast-follow line.
